In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir of Surah al-Rum

It is Meccan.

His Exalted saying: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾. We have already explained it, and the more sound view is that its meaning here is oath.

And His saying: ﴿The Romans have been defeated﴾, meaning: "The Romans have indeed been defeated" — so the oath falls upon this statement. The scholars of the Arabic language say that "qad" (قد) may be omitted in speech. The poet said:

(You burdened me with the sin of a man, and abandoned him,
like the mangy camel that cauterizes others while it grazes.)

Meaning: "Indeed, you have burdened me."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿in the nearest land﴾. Al-Adna (the nearest) means al-aqrab (the closest). Its meaning: the nearest to the land of Persia within the land of the Romans, so said Mujahid. It is al-Jazira (the Jazira), and it is the region between the Tigris and the Euphrates, called al-Jazira, of which [cities are] Harran, Rahbat Malik ibn Tawq, al-Raqqa, al-Ruha, and other than these.

And His saying: ﴿and after their defeat, they will overcome﴾. Its meaning: that the Romans, after the Persians' victory over them, will be victorious. If it is said: He said ﴿after their defeat﴾, but they were the ones defeated and not the ones who defeated? The answer to this: He mentioned their defeat, and what is meant by it is the victory of others over them. He attributed the defeat to them because that defeat reached them, and the reaching of the defeat to them is the falling of the defeat upon them. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they give food in spite of their love for it﴾, and food is not the one who has love; rather the human being is the one who has love, but it is attributed to the food because the love for it attaches to him. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is for one who fears standing before Me and fears My threat﴾, and the standing belongs to the servant, except that He attributed it [to Himself] because he stands before the hands of Allah, so it is connected to Allah in this respect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿in a few years﴾. Concerning al-bid' (a few, usually taken as three to nine), there are two opinions: the first is from one up to ten; the second is from three up to seven.

Likewise, the opinion differs concerning al-nayf (the excess above a round number). Some of them said: from one up to three; and some of them said: from one up to nine.

As for the occasion of revelation of the verse, Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "There was a continuous fighting between Persia and the Byzantines. The polytheists used to wish that Persia would defeat the Byzantines, and the Muslims used to wish that the Byzantines would defeat Persia, because they were People of the Book. He said: Persia defeated the Byzantines once, and the polytheists gloated over the Muslims and said: 'We will defeat you just as Persia defeated the Byzantines.' The Muslims came to the Prophet and mentioned that to him, and he said: 'Indeed, the Byzantines will defeat Persia.' The Companions of the Prophet said: 'When will that be?' He said: 'In a few years.' And Allah the Exalted revealed this verse."

He said: Abu Bakr came to Ubayy ibn Khalaf and mentioned that to him, and he said: "By Allah, the Byzantines will never defeat Persia." Then he said to Abu Bakr: "Shall I wager with you?" He said: "Yes," and he wagered with him over she-camels. They differed over the number of the she-camels: some of them said it was six, and it was said it was seven, and it was said other than that. And they set the term at five years.

Qatadah said: "This was at a time before gambling had been prohibited."

Abu Bakr came to the Prophet and mentioned that to him, and the Prophet said to him: "O Abu Bakr, increase the wager and extend the term." So he increased the number of she-camels and made the term seven years. Then the Byzantines prevailed over Persia and recovered the lands of al-Jazirah, al-Sham and other territories from Persia, for the Persians had seized all of them, and they took their greatest cross; they recovered these lands and recovered their cross, and defeated Persia.

They differed about the time of that: some of them said it was the Day of Badr, and some of them said it was the year of al-Hudaybiyah.

In some tafsir works: when Abu Bakr intended the Hijrah, he came to Ubayy ibn Khalaf and asked him for a guarantor for the she-camels, so his son 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr stood surety for them. Then, when Ubayy ibn Khalaf went out to Uhud, 'Abd al-Rahman asked him for a guarantor, and his son stood surety for the she-camels. Then, when the Byzantines prevailed over Persia, Abu Bakr took the she-camels.

In some narrations: the term was five years with no extension, and the five years passed and the Byzantines had not defeated Persia, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf took the she-camels. Then after that the Byzantines prevailed over Persia.

This verse is one of the miracles of the Prophet, because he reported about the unseen, which no one knows except Allah, and the matter was as he reported.

And His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after﴾, i.e., before their defeat and after their defeat.

And His saying: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah﴾, i.e., Allah grants victory to the People of the Book over those other than the People of the Book, and they rejoiced at that for the truthfulness of Allah the Exalted's promise; and because they said: "Just as Allah granted victory to the People of the Book over those other than the People of the Book, so too will He grant us victory over you."

And His saying: ﴿He helps whom He wills﴾, i.e., whom He wills of His servants.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, i.e., the Overpowering over His affair, the Bestower of favour upon His servants.

God's promise: "God does not break His promise" (Qur'an 30:6). Al-Sam'ani says: "His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God's promise; God does not break His promise﴾ — meaning: this victory is from God's promise, and God does not break His promise. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ that God's promise is true."

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the life of this world﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: [it means] their livelihood and their dealings in this world, that is, when they sow, when they reap, when they plant, and when they build. Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: the building of houses, the planting of trees, the digging of rivers, and the conducting of trade. It is related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Indeed one of them can count out dirhams with the tip of his fingernail and mention their weight without error, yet he does not know how to pray."

And His saying: ﴿and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾. The first "hum" is a beginning (mubtada᾽), and the second "hum" is another beginning, and its meaning is: they are heedless and unmindful of the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 8:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾. That is, for justice. It is also said: for the establishment of the truth. And it was said: for the truth.

It has been narrated in some reports that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a people who were reflecting, and he said: "Reflect upon the creation of God, and do not reflect upon God." This is a strange (gharib) report.

His words: ﴿and a specified term﴾. That is, and the duration of its appointed time. The scholars differed concerning this appointed term. Some of them said: it is the Hour. Others said: it is the time at which their destruction was decreed.

His words: ﴿Indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾. That is, deniers. The meeting with their Lord is the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land and looked to see what was the end of those before them?﴾ He means: the nations who passed away.

And His saying: ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾, i.e., more numerous than them in strength.

And His saying: ﴿And they stirred up the earth﴾, i.e., they ploughed the earth.

And His saying: ﴿And they cultivated it more than these have cultivated it﴾, i.e., they cultivated the earth more than the people of Makkah have cultivated it. He only said this because the people of Makkah did not have tillage.

And His saying: ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with evidences.

And His saying: ﴿So Allah was not one to wrong them﴾, i.e., to diminish their rights; but they diminished and cheated them of their rights.

[And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾.]

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 10:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was evil﴾ — that is, those who disbelieved. And His words: ﴿as-sūʾā (the evil)﴾ is Jahannam (Hell), and we seek refuge in Allah. Al-A'mash recited: "Then the end of those who did evil was the evil (al-sawʾ)." It has also been said: as-sūʾā means the ugliness of the outcome.

From this is the saying: "Sawāʾ walūd khayrun min ḥasnāʾ ʿaqīm" (an ugly woman who bears many children is better than a beautiful woman who is barren). That is, an ugly woman who bears children is better than a beautiful barren woman.

And His words: ﴿because they denied the signs of Allah﴾ — that is, because they denied the signs of Allah.

And His words: ﴿and they used to mock them﴾ — that is, they used to mock the signs of Allah.
Allah's words, "Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned" (Qur'an 30:11). The apparent meaning is clear, and we have already explained it.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be in despair.﴾ That is: the criminals will despair. It is also said: (they will fall silent) and their argument will be cut off. The poet said:

(O friend, do you recognize a worn-out trace? He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it has become desolate.)

Mujahid said: "Yubslis al-mujrimun" means they will be disgraced. It was also said: they will be bewildered."

And His saying: ﴿And there will be for them no intercessors from their associates﴾, meaning: the idols which they had taken as associates of God.

And His saying: ﴿And they will be, in their associates, disbelievers﴾, meaning: they will disbelieve in the idols and disown them on the Day of Resurrection. And the meaning of "kānū" (they were) is: "ṣārū" (they became).

"And on the Day when the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated (into groups)." That is, the people of Paradise will be distinguished from the people of the Fire. It was also said that its meaning is: He will separate the people of disobedience from the people of obedience, so He will punish the people of sins and bestow favor upon the obedient. And it is related from Qatadah that he said: "It is a separation with no gathering after it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 15:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, made joyful.﴾ "Rawda" (meadow) is a garden that is at the peak of freshness and beauty.

Al-Ta'i said: "Indeed, joy is a meadow, so when it is a hill [rabwa], it becomes a garden and a pool."

As for His words ﴿yuhbarun﴾ (made joyful), it means: they will be honored and given bounties. From it comes the word "khibra" (fine quality) for beautiful cloth. It is related from Yahya ibn Kathir that he said: "Yuhbarun" is listening to music in Paradise. Ibn Qutayba mentioned the meaning of His words ﴿yuhbarun﴾ as: they will be delighted.

﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ means: the resurrection (al-Ba'th) on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah).

And His saying: ﴿then they will be in the punishment, brought forth﴾ means: they will be punished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 17:

His words: ﴿Glorify God⦅ ﴾ — it has been explained that subhan Allah (Subhan Allah, "Glory be to God") means exalting God and declaring Him free of every imperfection.

It is related from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "It is a name of prohibition (imtinaʿ), which no created being may claim."

His words: ﴿Subhan Allah﴾ meaning: glorify God.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Every instance of tasbih (tasbih, glorification) in the Qur'an has the meaning of prayer (salah)."

In some reports: "The Prophet was asked about the best speech, and he said: Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih (Glory be to God and praise be to Him)."

It is established through the narration of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "Two words, light on the tongue, heavy in the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih, Subhan Allah al-ʿAzim (Glory be to God and praise be to Him; Glory be to God the Mighty)." This is the last report that al-Bukhari mentioned in the Sahih. He, may God be pleased with him, said: This hadith was related to us in its own wording by Karimah bint Ahmad in Mecca, who said: Abu al-Haytham informed us, al-Firabri informed us, al-Bukhari informed us with its chain (isnad) from Abu Hurayrah... the report.

In some traditions: "Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih is the prayer of the inhabitants of the heavens and the prayer of all creation."

His words: ﴿when you enter the evening﴾ meaning: when you enter the evening (masa').

His words: ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ meaning: when you enter the morning (sabah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth﴾. Ad-Dahhak said: "Al-hamd lillah (praise be to Allah) is the cloak of the Most Merciful (al-Rahman)."

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), through the narration of ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), that when the Prophet (ﷺ) raised his head from bowing (ruku'), he said: "Allah hears those who praise Him. Our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling whatever is between them, and filling whatever else You will after that. O Possessor of praise and glory, the most rightful thing a servant says, and we are all Your servants: none can withhold what You have given, and none can give what You have withheld, and no fortune-holder's fortune can benefit him against You."

And His saying: ﴿And in the evening﴾, meaning: pray to Allah in the evening.

And His saying: ﴿And when you enter midday﴾, meaning: you enter into the time of midday (zuhr). In the verse there is an indication of the five times of prayer. His saying: ﴿when you enter the evening﴾ is an indication of the Maghrib and ʿIsha' prayers; His saying: ﴿when you enter the morning﴾ is an indication of the Subh (dawn) prayer; His saying: ﴿and in the evening﴾ is an indication of the ʿAsr prayer.

And His saying: ﴿and when you enter midday﴾ is an indication of the Zuhr prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 19:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living﴾. We have already explained its meaning earlier; it is the bringing forth of the chick from the egg and the bringing forth of the egg from the hen, the bringing forth of the unbeliever from the believer and the believer from the unbeliever, and other such things.

His saying: ﴿And He revives the earth after its death﴾, meaning: just as He revived the earth after its death, so will He revive you after your death. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And thus you will be brought forth﴾.

Some of them said: He brings forth the dull-witted from the intelligent, and the intelligent from the dull-witted.

Al-Zuhri narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon one of his wives, and with her was Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth. He said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'She is Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Yaghuth.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah! He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living.'" And the woman was righteous, while her father had been an unbeliever.

Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust﴾, meaning: He created your origin from dust, and that is Adam, upon whom be the blessings of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾, meaning: you come and go, and it is said: (tanshatun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 21:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is that He created Eve from the rib of Adam. The second opinion: its meaning is that He created for you spouses from your own kind, and women are of the same kind as men, since they are all from the children of Adam.

His words: ﴿that you may find tranquility in them﴾ have the same meaning as His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And from it He created its mate so that he might find tranquility in her﴾, that is, so that he might find comfort with her.

His words: ﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾. Al-mawaddah (affection) is love and tenderness. Between spouses there may arise tenderness and affection that do not arise between relatives. It is related from Mujahid, al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah that they said: al-mawaddah is sexual intercourse (al-wat') and al-rahmah is the child.

His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾. Tafakkur (reflection) is the seeking of the meaning of things in matters that relate to the heart.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 22:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues and your colours﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: the difference of tongues is the difference of languages. So the Persians have a language, the Romans have a language, the Turks have a language, the Arabs have a language, and what is similar to this.

Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar, the Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of Israelite narratives) mentioned that God Most High divided seventy-two languages among the people: to the sons of Sam, nineteen languages; to the sons of Ham, seventeen languages; and the rest to the sons of Japheth. As for the difference of colours, it is that this one is red, this one is black, this one is white, and what is similar to this.

The second opinion: the difference of tongues is the difference of tones (naghmat), so that no two people share one identical tone. The difference of colours is known among people, even if they are all white or all black, for no two colours agree in every respect. In this there is a great wisdom: for if the colours and the tongues were the same, distinction would be lost. A father would not recognise his son, nor a son his father, and likewise among brothers, spouses, and all people.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who know﴾. Hafs ibn 'Asim recited "lil-'alimin" (for those who know), which is the plural of 'alim (one who knows). As for the well-known reading, "lil-'alimin" (for the worlds), it means: the jinn, mankind, and all creation.

God's words: "And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty." That is, your sleep by night and your seeking of His bounty by day. It is also said that the meaning is: among His signs is your sleep and your occupation with the bounty of God, by night and by day.

His words: "Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear." That is, who listen to what is mentioned to them of these signs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 24:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning﴾ mean: among His signs is that He shows you the lightning. The explanation of the matter concerning lightning has already been given. It is related from some of them that he said: "When the sky flashes forty times, it does not fail (yukhlifuhu), that is, the rain does not delay." The poet said:

(Let it not be a lightning like a lightning that is empty (khulbā)... Indeed the best of lightning is that which is accompanied by the rain.)

As for His words: ﴿with fear and hope﴾, that is: fear for the traveller, and hope for the resident. It is also said: fear of the thunderbolts, and hope for the rain.

As for His words: ﴿And He sends down water from the sky, and thereby revives the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their reason﴾, the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 25:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. One of them: its meaning is that they both exist by His command. The second opinion: their standing continues by His command. He raised up the heaven without pillars, and that continued until its appointed term, and it is by His command.

And His words: ﴿Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth﴾. It was said: the call is from the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). And it is said: it is from the heaven. The call is the call of Israfil (Isrāfīl, the angel of the Trumpet).

And His words: ﴿from the earth﴾, meaning: He calls you to come forth from the earth. This is according to the opinion which says that the call is from the heaven.

And His words: ﴿Then, behold, you come forth﴾ — we have already mentioned it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 26:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾. That is: obedient. It is also said: acknowledging servitude (muqarrabun bil-ubudiyyah).

And His words ﴿To Him belongs﴾ mean: to Him belongs dominion and creation. If it is said: if we take qunut (devout obedience) to mean obedience, then not everyone in the heavens and the earth obeys Him! The answer: obedience here does not carry the sense of worshipful obedience (ta'at al-'ibadah). Rather, obedience here carries the sense of submission (inqiyad), the yielding of every thing to that for which it was created.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 27:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He it is who originates creation﴾, meaning: He brings creation into being. ﴿Then He repeats it﴾, meaning: He gives you life after He causes you to die.

And His saying: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾. If it is said: How can His saying ﴿and it is easier for Him﴾ be correct, when nothing is difficult for God? The answer to this: the meaning of His saying ﴿and it is easier for Him﴾ is: it is easy for Him. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "And it is easy for Him." Al-Farazdaq said in verse:

(Indeed He who raised the sky, built for us a house whose pillars are mighty and lofty.)

(The house of Zurara is enclosed in its courtyard, and Mujashi' and Abu al-Fawaris Nahshal.)

And His saying "a'azz wa atwal" (mighty and lofty) means 'azīza wa ṭawīla (mighty and lofty in feminine form, agreeing with the noun). Another poet said:

(By your life, I do not know, and indeed I am fearful, over which of us death will first attack.)

Meaning: (fearful, wajil). The second opinion regarding the verse is that its meaning is: it is easier for Him according to what occurs to their minds, for what occurs to the minds of created beings is that repetition is easier than initiation. It is also said that its meaning is: it is easier for the creatures, because whoever begins something that is hard for him, when he repeats it a second time, it becomes easier and simpler.

And His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest likeness﴾, meaning: the highest attribute. The highest attribute is that He has no partner and ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾, as related from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: the highest attribute is that there is no god but Allah.

And His saying: ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: this is an attribute of Him in the sight of the people of the heavens and the earth.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: the Mighty in respect of retribution, the Wise in respect of management.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 28:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves﴾, i.e., a likeness from your own example. Then He mentioned the likeness, saying: ﴿Do you have, from among what your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided you with?﴾ Its meaning: Do you have partners from among your slaves in your wealth, who share with you in it? So if you do not accept this for yourselves, how do you accept it for Me and attribute it to Me?

His saying: ﴿in what We have provided you with﴾, i.e., in what We have given you of provision and wealth.

His saying: ﴿so that you are equal in it﴾ is a reference to what we have said.

His saying: ﴿you fear them as you fear one another﴾, i.e., you fear their sharing with you in your wealth as you fear [the sharing of] your like, and that is a free partner with a free partner. Here "anfusakum" (ourselves/yourselves) carries the meaning of "amthalakum" (your like). There is another opinion, stated by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that the verse was revealed concerning the talbiyah of the polytheists, for they used to say: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am. You have no partner except a partner who belongs to You; You possess him and what he possesses."

His saying: ﴿you fear them as you fear one another﴾, i.e., you fear them in blame as you fear the blame of your like.

His saying: ﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reason﴾, i.e., who contemplate these proofs with their intellects.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 29:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿But those who did wrong follow their own desires without knowledge.﴾ Al-Ahwa' (the desires) is the plural of al-hawa, and al-hawa is what a person desires. It is related from some of them: "Al-hawa is the greatest object of worship."

His statement: ﴿without knowledge﴾ means: they followed their desires in ignorance of what is obligatory upon them.

His statement: ﴿So who can guide one whom Allah has led astray?﴾ means: whom Allah has led astray.

﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be to the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.﴾

His statement: ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ means: they will have none who prevents them from Our punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 30:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾ means: devote your religion to God. Setting the face is the same as setting the religion, and we have already explained the meaning of ḥanīf (one who turns away from falsehood toward truth).

And His saying: ﴿the natural disposition (fiṭrah) of God, upon which He created mankind﴾. As for the fiṭrah being put in the accusative, it is by way of incitement (ighrā'), meaning: hold fast to the fiṭrah of God upon which He created mankind. The scholars differed concerning this fiṭrah. Some of them said that fiṭrah here means religion (dīn).

His saying: ﴿upon which He created mankind﴾ means: He created mankind upon it. This view is attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, al-Kalbi, Muqatil and others. And it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every child is born upon the fiṭrah, and his parents make him a Jew or a Christian."

It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said, relating from his Lord: "I created My servants as ḥunafā' (monotheists), and the devils led them astray from their religion."

If it is said: How does this accord with your principles, since you hold that God Exalted created mankind in two categories, believers and disbelievers? This verse and these reports indicate that God Exalted created His servants as believers. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that God Exalted brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins and addressed them with His words: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ and they acknowledged servitude and faith; thus people are born upon that. The answer to this: the people of knowledge differed on this. Al-Nahhas in his tafsir related from Ibn al-Mubarak that the verse refers to believers specifically. Abu (‘Ubayd) in Gharib al-Hadith related from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan that he said: this was before the revelation of the rulings and the command to jihad, as if he indicated that the verse is abrogated. Then al-Nahhas mentioned that both meanings are weak.

As for what Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned, it is merely a restriction without evidence for it; and as for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan mentioned, it is the affirmation of abrogation in reports, and reports are not subject to abrogation. The correct meaning of the verse and the report is that the meaning of fiṭrah is that every person is born in such a way that, when asked, "Who created you?", he says, "God created me." This is the knowledge that occurs in the original creation.

Abu (‘Ubayd) al-Harawi said: it is the knowledge of innate disposition and nature, and to this the indication in His saying is made: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, God﴾. By this degree alone the commanded faith is not attained. So people are created upon this fiṭrah. As for the reality of faith and the reality of disbelief, people are divided into two categories concerning them, as the Book and the Sunnah have stated. Al-Zajjaj and al-Nahhas said: this is the view of the people of the Sunnah. This view is also the choice of Ibn Qutaybah.

His saying: ﴿There is no alteration of the creation of God﴾, according to this view, means: no one returns to himself without knowing that he has a god and a creator.

The second view concerning the verse is that the fiṭrah of God here means the religion of God; people are born upon the covenant that was taken from them on the Day of the Covenant, and this is the fiṭrah of God. This view is reported from al-Awza'i and Hammad ibn Salamah.

It has also come in the report we narrated, namely his saying: "Every child is born upon the fiṭrah, and his parents make him a Jew or a Christian, just as an animal gives birth to an animal. Do you notice any mutilation in it?" Then he said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿the natural disposition of God upon which He created mankind﴾."

He, may God be pleased with him, said: We were informed of this hadith in the wording of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us, al-Ghadafari informed us, al-Dabari informed us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ)... the hadith.

There is a third view concerning the verse: what Abu 'Ubayd al-Harawi narrated in al-Gharibayn from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: His saying "upon the fiṭrah" means: upon the initial creation in which a person is formed in the womb, whether for happiness or misery; "his parents make him a Jew" means: in the rulings of this world. Many scholars of the meanings have affirmed what we mentioned earlier, namely that the verse refers specifically to Muslims, and this is a generality used in the sense of a particularity.

His saying: ﴿There is no alteration of the creation of God﴾ has several views: first, what we explained earlier; second, there is no alteration of the creation of God, meaning the happy one does not become wretched, nor the wretched one happy, once he has been created upon one of them; third, there is no alteration of the creation of God, meaning no one can be like the creation of God, and its meaning is that there is no creator other than Him.

It is related from 'Ikrimah that he said: ﴿There is no alteration of the creation of God﴾ is the prohibition of castration.

The scholars differed on this. Some prohibited it in all cases; some permitted it for all animals except humans; and some permitted it for all animals except horses, because it cuts off offspring, and offspring is sought in horses more than in other animals. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The best property is a row of pollinated palms and a horse that is frequently bred." The "pollinated row" (sikkah ma'burah) is a row of palm trees that have been pollinated, and "frequently bred" (mo'murah) refers to a mare that bears much offspring.

As for when we take fiṭrah to mean religion, His saying: ﴿There is no alteration of the creation of God﴾ is a report with the meaning of a command, as if He said: do not alter the religion of God. It has come in a report: fiṭrah in the sense of the word of Islam.

Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you lies down on his bed and says: 'O God, I have submitted myself to You, I have entrusted my affair to You, I have turned my back to You, there is no refuge nor escape from You except to You; I believed in Your Book which You sent down, and in Your Prophet whom You sent,' then if he dies, he dies upon the fiṭrah."

The word fiṭrah has also come in the sense of sunnah, as in the well-known report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ten are of the fiṭrah," meaning: of the sunnah, the report.

His saying: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ means: the straight religion; it is also said: the straight reckoning.

His saying: ﴿But most people do not know﴾ is clear in meaning. They recited, regarding fiṭrah, the verse of Ka'b ibn Malik in poetry:

(If you kill us, the religion of God is our fiṭrah...
and killing in the right, in the sight of God, is a distinction.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Turning penitently to Him﴾, i.e., follow the religion of God, ﴿turning penitently to Him﴾, i.e., returning (rāji'īn) to Him. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: returning to God through your prayers and your deeds. And it is related from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani that he said: the penitent (munīb) is the one who walks upon the earth while his heart is with God. If it is said: how does His saying ﴿turning penitently﴾ fit, when He addressed one person at the beginning, namely the Messenger, with His saying ﴿So set your face toward the religion, upright (ḥanīfan)﴾? The answer to this is that His saying ﴿So set your face﴾ means: set your face, and your community with you, turning penitently to God. The real meaning is: follow the upright religion, turning penitently to God.

And His saying: ﴿And fear Him, and establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists﴾, i.e., the deniers (al-jāḥidīn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Of those who split up their religion and became sects﴾ means: they abandoned their religion. It has also been read as "farraqū dīnahum" (they divided their religion), meaning: they split into factions regarding their religion. Concerning this verse, I say, the most apparent of the opinions is that what is meant by them are the Jews and the Christians.

It has been related in some reports: "The Jews split into seventy-one sects, the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one."

The second opinion: what is meant by the verse is the Khawarij. This is narrated from Abu Umamah al-Bahili.

The third opinion: what is meant by the verse is the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') and innovations (ahl al-bid'ah). This has been related in a continuous (musnad) report from 'Ā'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Those who split up their religion and became sects are the people of desires and innovations from this Ummah. O 'Ā'ishah, every people has a repentance except the people of desires and innovations; there is no repentance for them. I am free of them, and they are free of me."

His saying: ﴿Every faction, rejoicing in what they have﴾ means: pleased with what is with them. Some of the scholars of the language said: "al-hizb" (faction) means "the helper," and the poet said: "Am kayfa akhnū wa-Bilāl ḥizbī..." meaning: my helpers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 33:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And when harm touches mankind﴾, meaning: hardship.

And His words: ﴿they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾, meaning: turning back to Him in supplication. Its meaning is that when they fall into hardship, they abandon calling upon the idols and call upon God alone.

And His words: ﴿then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, meaning: He removes the hardship from them by His mercy.

And His words: ﴿behold, a party of them associate others with their Lord﴾, meaning: they returned to the root of their polytheism.

His Exalted saying: ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾. We have already explained this before.

And His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾. This is in the form of a command (*amr*) but with the meaning of a threat (*tahdid*). Ibn Mas'ud recited: "وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون" (*wa-liyatamatta'u fa-sawfa ya'lamun*), meaning "And let them enjoy themselves, for they will soon know."

Verse 30:35 of the Qur'an, in al-Sam'ani's commentary:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority (sultan), so that it speaks of what they used to associate with Him?﴾ That is, a proof and an excuse. It is also said: "Or have We sent down to them an authority" means a book that speaks of their polytheism, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿so that it speaks of what they used to associate with Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾, meaning: fertility and abundant rain. It is also said: security and well-being.

And His saying: ﴿they rejoice in it﴾. Here "rejoicing" (al-fari') means the rejoicing of arrogance (farah al-batar) and neglect of gratitude.

And His saying: ﴿but if an evil befalls them﴾, meaning: drought and scarcity of rain. It is also said: fear and affliction.

And His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forth﴾, meaning: because of sins.

And His saying: ﴿behold, they despair﴾, meaning: they lose hope. This is a sign of those who are not believers. As for the sign of the believers, it is thanking God at the time of blessing and hoping for relief at the time of hardship.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that God extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it?﴾

And His saying: ﴿and restricts﴾, i.e., constricts.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾, i.e., who affirm.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So give to the near of kin his right﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by giving to the near of kin here is maintaining the ties of kinship (silat al-rahim) through gifts and presents. Qatadah said: "Whoever does not give to his relatives, and walks to them on his own feet, has severed his kinship." Some have applied the verse to giving to the near of kin of the Messenger.

His saying: ﴿and the needy﴾, meaning: the one who goes about (al-tawwaf).

His saying: ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, meaning: the traveler. It was also said: the guest.

It is authentically related that the Prophet said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest."

It is also related from him, upon him be prayer and peace, that he said: "Hospitality is for three days, and the gift (jaizah) is for one day and night."

Malik said: The meaning of the gift (al-jaizah) is that one exerts himself for him during one day and night; as for what is beyond that, one sets forth to him whatever is at hand.

His saying: ﴿That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah﴾, meaning: they seek the good pleasure of Allah.

His saying: ﴿And those are the successful﴾, meaning: the triumphant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 39:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whatever you give in usury (riba) so that it may increase within the wealth of people﴾. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that the meaning of the verse is that a man gives another a gift so that he will give him more than it. This is permissible for people to do, except that on the Day of Resurrection no reward is given for it. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿so it does not increase with Allah﴾. This act was forbidden for the Prophet, as Allah the Exalted said to him: ﴿and do not give seeking to receive more﴾, meaning: do not give while seeking to be given more than what you gave.

And on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said: A man would give his friend wealth so that the friend's wealth would increase, and he did not intend thereby the Face of Allah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them.

It is also read: "li-yarbu fi amwal al-nas" (so that it may increase in the wealth of people). "fa-la yarbu 'inda Allah" (so it does not increase with Allah), meaning: it does not increase with Allah.

His words: ﴿And whatever you give in zakat﴾, meaning: charity (sadaqa).

His words: ﴿seeking the Face of Allah﴾ — we have already explained this.

His words: ﴿Then those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward)﴾, meaning: those who possess multiples (of reward).

The Arabs say: "al-qawm musminun wa muhzilun wa mulbinun" (the people have become fat, lean, and milch-owning), and the meaning is what we have explained. The poet said: ((He informs them with caution, and they said: "Build your ... in the shade of a sword-bearer")), meaning: one who possesses a sword.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life﴾, the verse is clear in its meaning.

And His saying: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?﴾ That is: is there anything of the like of that?

And His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ — we have already explained it before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 41:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾ concerning the verse. I say: One of them is what is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "The corruption on the land is the killing by one of the two sons of Adam of his brother, and the corruption in the sea is the seizure of ships by the king. Both are in the Qur'an."

And from al-Dahhak, who said: "The earth was green, blossoming, fresh and pleasant. Whenever a son of Adam came to a tree, he would find fruit on it. The water of the sea was sweet. The lion did not prey on cattle or sheep, nor did the cat seek the mouse, and the like of that. When one of the sons of Adam killed his brother, the earth shuddered, the trees became thorny, the water of the sea became salty and bitter, and the animals began to attack one another."

The second opinion regarding the verse is that what is meant by corruption on the land is drought and famine, and corruption in the sea is the scarcity of rain. If it is said: "What corruption is there in the scarcity of rain in the sea and on the land?" We say: As for the land, it is the appearance of hardship and famine. As for the sea, they have said: when rain does not fall on the sea, the creatures of the sea become blind, and it is said: when rain does not fall on the sea, the shells become empty of pearls, for when rain falls the oyster rises to the surface of the sea, opens its mouth, and whatever falls into it becomes a pearl.

The third opinion regarding the verse, and it is the most apparent, is that "the land" refers to the open country and the desert, and "the sea" refers to the towns and cities. The Arabs call every village or city situated on flowing water a "sea."

As for His words: ﴿by what the hands of people have earned﴾, meaning: by what they have committed of sins. God, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven﴾.

As for His words: ﴿that He may let them taste part of what they have done, so that they may return﴾, meaning: that they may return to God in repentance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 30, verse 42:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Travel through the land and see what was the end of those before you﴾, meaning: the final outcome of those who were before.

And His saying: ﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾, meaning: in God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 43:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾. That is: aim toward the direction of the upright religion. It was also said: make your deeds straight for the upright religion. It is also said: remain steadfast upon the upright religion.

And His saying: ﴿before there comes a Day which has no means of turning back﴾. That is: the Resurrection, which no one can turn back from Allah.

And His saying: ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾. That is: they will separate into a group in the Garden and a group in the Blaze.

The poet said:

(And we were like the two companions of Judhayma for a span of time, until it was said they would never part [yatasadda'a].)

That is: they would never separate (yatafarraqa).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 44:

And His the Exalted's saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, meaning: the burden (wabal) of his disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteousness, it is for their own selves that they prepare [a resting place]﴾, meaning: they make ready the resting places (yumahhidun, from al-muwattiʾun al-madaji'), and it is said: they spread out the bedding (yabsitun al-furush). The poet said:

(Prepare for yourself before illness and destruction come upon you... and do not neglect a soul that has no successor.)
And His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 30, verse 46:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news﴾. Al-rih (the wind): a subtle body that moves through the air to the right and to the left, following the arrangement of its movements in its directions, and it cannot be grasped because of its subtlety.

It is related from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: The winds are four for mercy and four for punishment, and their total is eight. Those for mercy are: the mubashshirat (bearers of good news), the nashirat (spreaders), the dhariyat (scatterers), and the mursalat (sent forth). Those for punishment are: the 'aqim (barren), the sarsar (the furious) on land, the 'asif (the violent), and the qasif (the crashing) at sea.

His words: ﴿that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, i.e., the rain. It is also said: the pleasant quality of the wind and its delight.

His words: ﴿and that the ships may sail by His command﴾, i.e., that the ships may sail on the sea by these winds through His command.

His words: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, i.e., that you may seek of the bounty of Allah, may He be exalted, through trade on the sea.

His words: ﴿and that you may be grateful﴾, meaning: that you may be grateful to Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We indeed sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs﴾. That is: with evidences (al-dalalat).

And His saying: ﴿So We took retribution against those who committed crime﴾. That is: they committed crime by denying (the messengers).

And His saying: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾. That is: the aid of the believers by saving them. It was also said: the aid of the believers by defending them and warding off punishment [from them].

And in some of the chains of narration, through the transmission of Umm al-Darda', the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever defends the honour (ghars) of his Muslim brother, it is incumbent upon Allah to ward off the Fire from him on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 48:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, meaning: they spread the clouds. And in some of the tafsirs it is mentioned that Allah, the Exalted, sends a wind that stirs up the earth into dust, then sends a wind that gathers the clouds together with rain. This is the meaning of the verse.

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So He spreads them across the sky however He wills﴾, meaning: a journey of a day, or two days, or more, as He wills.

And His saying: ﴿and makes them into fragments﴾, meaning: pieces.

And His saying: ﴿so you see the rain coming out from within them﴾. Al-Dahhak recited "min khilalihi" (من خلله). Al-wadq (الودق) means the rain. The poet said:

(So no cloud has poured its rain, and no land has brought forth its herbage through its rain...)

It was also said: al-wadq is the lightning, but the first view is more evident.

And His saying: ﴿Then when He causes it to strike whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾, meaning: some of them give good news to one another.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 49:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, they were, before it was sent down to them, before that, utterly despairing.﴾ That is: hopeless (āyisīn). And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And indeed they were, before it was sent down to them, before that, utterly despairing," with "nunazzila" (we sent down) in place of "yunazzila" (it was sent down).

If it is said: What is the meaning of the repetition of His saying ﴿before﴾ here, and what benefit is there in it? The answer to this is in two respects. The first: that it is for emphasis (ta'kid), and this is the view of most grammarians (ahl al-nahw), and the Arabs do much of this kind of thing. The second: that its meaning is: "before" the clouds, and "before" the sending down of the rain; so the one (of the two) refers to the sending down of the rain, and the other refers to the producing of the clouds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 30, verse 50:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy﴾. It was also read as "athar rahmat Allah" (the trace of Allah's mercy). Al-athar (the traces) is the plural of al-athar (the trace), and al-athar carries the meaning of al-athar (the traces).

And His words: ﴿how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, meaning: how Allah gives life to the earth with rain after its death? For He gives life to the dead on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them have said: "He gives life to the earth after its death" means the heedless hearts with the light of knowledge, certainty and exegesis (tafsir).

And His words: ﴿and He is over all things Powerful﴾, meaning: Capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 51:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾ have two interpretations. The first: they saw the wind as yellow, and if the wind were in this form it would not benefit them. The second view, which is the well-known one: "they saw it turned yellow," meaning they saw the crops turned yellow.

As for His words: ﴿they would certainly continue disbelieving after it﴾, it is said: "Zalla fulan yaf'alu kadhā" (ẓalla, meaning "he kept doing such-and-such"), that is, "ja'ala yaf'alu kadhā" (he began/kept doing such-and-such), and it is like their saying "aḍḥā fulan yaf'alu kadhā" (he came to be doing such-and-such). Except that the phrase ẓalla yaf'alu is customarily used for the whole of the day, while aḍḥā is used for the early part of the day.

As for His words: ﴿disbelieving﴾, that is, denying, and it was also said: they are ungrateful for the blessing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, and He placed them in the position of the dead, because they did not benefit from their lives.

And His saying: ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾. He placed them in the position of the deaf, because they did not benefit from their hearing.

And His saying: ﴿when they turn away, retreating﴾, i.e., turning away. If it is said: the deaf person does not hear whether he faces you or turns away, so what is the meaning of this statement? The answer to this: when he is facing you, if he does not hear, he can understand by gesture; but when he is turned away, he does not hear and does not understand by gesture.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their misguidance﴾, meaning: you cannot turn the blind away from their misguidance, and the blind are the disbelievers. It is also said: you cannot guide the blind out of their misguidance.

And His saying: ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, meaning: you do not make hear except those who believe in Our signs.

And His saying: ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 54:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. It is also recited as "min ḍaʿf" with both the fatḥa and the ḍamma, and both have the same meaning. The preferable reading is "min ḍaʿf" with the ḍamma, on the basis of what is related from ʿAṭiyya, who said: "I recited this verse to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, and I recited 'min ḍaʿf' with the naṣb (fatḥa). He said: 'min ḍuʿf' with the ḍamma, and he said: 'It was taken from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as you have taken it from me.'"

His saying: ﴿from weakness﴾ means: from a despised water. It has also been said: from one who possesses weakness.

His saying: ﴿then He made after weakness strength﴾ means: youth, which is the time of strength.

His saying: ﴿then He made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ refers to old age and hoariness. Gray hair (shayb) is the herald of death. The poet said:

(I saw gray hair as a messenger of the fates to its bearer, and enough for you is a warner.)

His saying: ﴿He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful﴾ — its meaning is clear.

The Almighty's words: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾ meaning: the criminals will take an oath.

And His words: ﴿they tarried not but an hour﴾ meaning: in their graves. It was also said: in the world. They said this out of the terror of what they saw of the Resurrection, so they forgot what had been before that.

And His words: ﴿Thus they were ever deluded﴾ meaning: they were turned away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 56:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge and faith will say: "You have indeed remained, according to the Book of God..."﴾ That is: according to the decree of God and His knowledge. The poet said:

(And [fate] turned away from the one who sought its favor, so you turned away... and that was not by God's decree, since He is the one who writes [it down].)

That is: decrees. It is also said that in the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, transposition of words), and its meaning is: "And those who have been given knowledge and faith will say: 'You have indeed remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.'"

And His words: ﴿This is the Day of Resurrection﴾ That is: the Resurrection (al-qiyamah).

And His words: ﴿But you did not know﴾ That is: you did not know that the Resurrection is true.

Allah's saying: ﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who wronged﴾. That is, their excuse. Al-ma'dhirah (excuse) is the showing of what removes blame.

And His saying: ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. That is, they will not be made to clarify themselves. It is also said: they will not be asked to seek forgiveness (al-'utbā).

The Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, meaning: every kind of likeness.

And His words: ﴿And if you should bring them a sign, those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are nothing but falsifiers"﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾. Ṭabʿ (sealing, stamping) and khatm (sealing) have one meaning, and it is that which prevents the heart from perceiving.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said:

"I seek refuge in God from greed that leads to a stamping (ṭabʿ)."

al-Aʿshā said:

(For him are crowns set with rubies, their excellence)
its cups are such that you see no flaw in them, nor any stamp (ṭabʿ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true.﴾ He means: the promise of the Resurrection.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady.﴾ That is: let them not hasten you (yastahjilanaka), for hastiness (khiffah) leads to ignorance. Its meaning is: let not those who have no certainty, and their followers, move you toward error. So Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to be patient in holding to the truth and to leave their followers in their misguidance, and not to lend an ear to their statements. It has been narrated that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was once praying when a man called out to him, saying, "There is no judgement except that of Allah," and the man was one of the Kharijites. So Ali recited in his prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady.﴾
